title: Mandible Interface Contract

commands.name: mandible issue report <id> [--json]
commands.description: Print deterministic issue context for handoff and planning.

commands.name: mandible issue title <id> [--json] [--graceful]
commands.description: Resolve an issue title for caller-supplied commit-message defaults. --graceful makes daemon-unreachable failures non-fatal.

commands.name: mandible umbrella status <id> [--deep] [--json]
commands.description: Print one deterministic coordinator fact packet: umbrella body/revision/head, latest delegation manifest, child summaries, parent-role holder state, and repo auth queue summary. Every head object carries both its own digest and an additive subtree_digest covering all transitive parent_child descendants. Child summaries include kind and child_count (direct parent_child children) so nested sub-umbrellas are visible without drilling in. --deep includes child bodies, latest closeouts/comments, branch/auth links, and issue state for parent resumption.

commands.name: mandible umbrella adopt <umbrella> <children...> [--json]
commands.description: Idempotently adopt explicit children into an umbrella, create missing parent_child edges, refresh the delegation-manifest checkpoint server-side, report body-table/link-graph drift, and return the updated umbrella status fact packet.

commands.name: mandible umbrella reconcile <umbrella> [--json]
commands.description: Derive children only from the canonical umbrella Children table, create missing parent_child edges, refresh the delegation-manifest checkpoint server-side, report reconciliation drift, and return the updated umbrella status fact packet.

commands.name: mandible umbrella manifest refresh <umbrella> [--json]
commands.description: Refresh the umbrella delegation-manifest checkpoint from current linked child issue heads server-side without changing parent_child edges, and return the updated umbrella status fact packet.

commands.name: mandible issue parent-role status|assume <umbrella> [--session <id>] [--mechanism <name>] [--override] [--json]
commands.description: Inspect or record advisory parent-role holder state; live holder conflicts require an explicit override while stale holders are informational.

commands.name: mandible issue heads <id>... [--json]
commands.description: Print issue state digests for delegation manifests and resume checks. Each head carries its own digest plus an additive subtree_digest over the issue and all transitive parent_child descendants (cycle-safe, each descendant once), so drift two or more levels down a nested umbrella is detectable.

commands.name: mandible issue changed --since-manifest <file> [--json]
commands.description: Compare current issue digests with a legacy saved delegation manifest file. Classifies each entry as changed (own digest drifted), subtree_changed (own stable, subtree digest drifted), unchanged, or unknown (manifest predates subtree digests, so subtree drift is indeterminate).

commands.name: mandible issue changed --since-issue <umbrella> [--kind delegation-manifest] [--checkpoint <id>] [--json]
commands.description: Compare current issue digests and the umbrella's own head with a structured checkpoint on an umbrella issue; omit --checkpoint to use the latest checkpoint. Classifies each entry as changed, subtree_changed, unchanged, or unknown; unknown means the manifest entry has no baseline subtree digest and never silently reports unchanged.

commands.name: mandible issue checkpoint add <issue-ref> --kind <kind> [--payload <json-or-> | --payload-file <file-or->]
commands.description: Append kind-tagged structured issue state outside the comment stream. Use --payload - or --payload-file - to read JSON from stdin.

commands.name: mandible issue checkpoint show <issue-ref> --kind <kind> [--latest|--all] [--json]
commands.description: Read kind-tagged structured issue state without parsing comments.

commands.name: mandible issue status <id> <none|in_progress|done|blocked|pivot-needed>
commands.description: Set worker coordination status without changing open/closed lifecycle status.

commands.name: mandible issue branch add <id> <branch> [--role primary|superseded]
commands.description: Link a branch to an issue as structured coordination state.

commands.name: mandible issue link <src> <target...> [--type t] [--note n]
commands.description: Create deliberate structured issue/comment relationship edges with shared action grouping for multi-target links. Accepted types: parent_child, blocks, duplicate_of, related, references, fixed_by, caused_by, implements, tests.

commands.name: mandible issue unlink <src> <target...> [--type t]
commands.description: Tombstone deliberate structured issue/comment relationship edges and emit relationship removal events. Accepted types: parent_child, blocks, duplicate_of, related, references, fixed_by, caused_by, implements, tests.

commands.name: mandible issue comment add <issue-ref> -m <text> [--reopen]
commands.description: Append rendered Markdown comments with real newline characters and return the issue lifecycle status; --reopen atomically reopens and comments.

commands.name: mandible issue comment edit <comment-ref> -m <body> [--base-revision <rev>] [--base-body-hash <hash>]
commands.description: Edit a comment body with optional stale-base checks; comment-ref accepts a raw comment id, <issue-ref>#<ordinal>, or <issue-ref>#last. Conflicts with a stale base return exit code 3.

commands.name: mandible issue description edit <issue-ref> -m <text>
commands.description: Edit issue descriptions while preserving body revision history.

commands.name: mandible issue label add|rm <id> <label>
commands.description: Mirror portable issue facts such as mandible:status:<value> labels.

commands.name: mandible auth list [--repo <repo>] [--head <branch>] [--base <branch>] [--status <status>] [--json]
commands.description: Find existing auth requests before submitting duplicates.

commands.name: mandible auth check [--branch <branch>] [--repo <repo>] [--target <branch>] [--json]
commands.description: Report whether a merge is clean against the target and queued pairwise-independent requests.

commands.name: mandible auth request <branch> --title <text> --issue <id> [--closes-issue <id>] [--message <text> | --message-file <file>] [--verification <text>] [--spec <text>] [--no-watch]
commands.description: Submit protected-branch auth work. Use --issue for reference context and --closes-issue only for intended closure. --message/--message-file supply the agent-authored canonical change message the merge commits verbatim; --verification fills its machine-owned Verification section (default "Not recorded") and is validated against the message at the daemon boundary.

commands.name: mandible auth replay-archives <request-id> [--json]
commands.description: Replay Codex thread archive attempts for a completed successful merge auth request without rerunning the merge or deferred issue actions.

commands.name: mandible work-unit claim --issue <id> --repo <repo> [--branch <branch>] [--parent-branch <branch>] [--kind solo|partition|integration] [--session <id>] [--graceful]
commands.description: Create or reuse a branch-based work unit using explicit mechanism inputs only. --graceful makes daemon-unreachable failures non-fatal.

commands.name: mandible work-unit activate --issue <id> --repo <repo> [--branch <branch>] [--session <id>] [--graceful]
commands.description: Mark the matching work unit committed, or auto-claim it in committed state, using explicit mechanism inputs only.

commands.name: mandible work-unit find --repo <repo> (--issue <id> | --branch <branch>) [--state <state>] [--graceful]
commands.description: Find work units by repo plus issue or branch, with optional state filtering.

commands.name: mandible work-unit resolve --id <work-unit-id> [--auth-request-id <id>] [--graceful]
commands.description: Patch a work unit to resolved after a successful merge, optionally linking the auth request.

commands.name: mandible work-unit release --issue <id> --repo <repo> [--graceful]
commands.description: Release active work units for an abandoned issue/repo lane without encoding worktree layout policy.

commands.name: mandible trash list|create|restore|gc
commands.description: List, snapshot/remove, restore, or expire reversible branch/worktree trash custody. Create accepts a canonical-project-resolvable ref and reports when the removed worktree path can no longer be used.

commands.name: mandible issue-file path [cwd]
commands.description: Resolve the git-root .issue helper file path for a caller-supplied or current working directory.

commands.name: mandible issue-file read [cwd]
commands.description: Read newline-delimited issue refs from the git-root .issue helper file. Blank lines and # comments are ignored.

commands.name: mandible issue-file write [--cwd <path>] <issue>...
commands.description: Write newline-delimited issue refs to the git-root .issue helper file for policy wrapper auto-discovery.

commands.name: mandible commit trailer [issue...]
commands.description: Render Mandible-Issue trailers for explicit issues, or from the nearest worktree .issue file when no issues are passed.

commands.name: mandible session link-issue <session-id> --issue <id> --repo <repo> [--repo-name <name>] [--graceful]
commands.description: Link an existing Mandible session to an issue/repo pair through the supported client surface.

commands.name: mandible conversations star <conversation-ref|--current> [--json]
commands.description: Star exactly one durable conversation resolved by exact conversation id, exact provider session id, or the ambient provider session.

commands.name: mandible conversations unstar <conversation-ref|--current> [--json]
commands.description: Unstar exactly one durable conversation resolved without prefix ambiguity.

commands.name: mandible conversations tag add <conversation-ref|--current> <tag...> [--json]
commands.description: Append ordered, trimmed, exact-case-deduplicated tags to one durable conversation.

commands.name: mandible conversations tag rm <conversation-ref|--current> <tag...> [--json]
commands.description: Remove exact-case tags from one durable conversation.

commands.name: mandible conversations comment <conversation-ref|--current> -m <markdown> [--json]
commands.description: Append Markdown to durable conversation notes with one blank-line separator; existing notes are never overwritten.

commands.name: mandible artifact ingest <path...> [--blob-only] [--json]
commands.description: Register a logical artifact version by default. --blob-only is the explicit low-level escape hatch for registering immutable bytes without a logical artifact/version identity.

commands.name: mandible artifact format <ref> [--as id|url|markdown|full] [--label <text>] [--json]
commands.description: Resolve an artifact identity and render its ambiguity-safe short ref by default, or an HTTP URL, Markdown hyperlink, full canonical id, or structured JSON.

commands.name: mandible instructions install [--target <file>] [--worktree <path>] [--force]
commands.description: Refresh configured instruction targets, or update one explicit target. Configured targets support managed-block and standalone modes; tracked protected-branch writes are refused unless --force is explicit.

commands.name: mandible instructions targets list|add|rm <path> [--mode managed-block|standalone]
commands.description: Configure where the generated Mandible instruction fragment is written.

commands.name: mandible instructions post-export get|set|clear <command>
commands.description: Configure an optional command to run after instruction targets refresh, such as a module compiler.

commands.name: mandible project list [--json]
commands.description: List canonical projects with keys, display names, remotes, checkouts, and issue counts.

commands.name: mandible project show <ref> [--json]
commands.description: Resolve a project by key, id, work_repo_id, checkout root, remote, or display name and print its registry record.

commands.name: mandible project add --key <k> [--display <name>] [--remote <url>] [--root <path>] [--namespace remote|upstream|local]
commands.description: Register a canonical project; optionally register its first checkout.

commands.name:
mandible project update [--key ] [--display ] [--remote ] [--namespace

]
commands.description: Update fields on an existing project registry entry.

commands.name: mandible project add-checkout <ref> --root <path> [--work-repo-id <id>] [--default-branch <b>]
commands.description: Register or update a checkout for a project.

commands.name: mandible project update-checkout --root <path> --project <ref> [--work-repo-id <id>] [--default-branch <b>]
commands.description: Update or register a checkout by root path, choosing its project.

commands.name: mandible project audit [--json]
commands.description: Read-only registry audit: duplicate display names, local projects, numbered path-derived repo ids, ambiguous roots, missing keys.

commands.name: mandible project repair [--apply] [--merge <src> <dst>] [--json]
commands.description: Guarded registry normalization: backfill keys and optionally merge duplicate projects (dry run unless --apply).

commands.name: mandible user setup [--slug <s>] [--name <n>] [--email <e>] [--agents] [--json]
commands.description: Idempotently create or update the local human operator and record its user id in settings; --agents deliberately provisions the built-in agent users and bindings. When GLOBAL git config sets user.signingkey and it resolves to a readable public key, setup also registers it as the operator's ssh_key credential (idempotent; never duplicates an active fingerprint), which protected-merge attestation requires; a key configured only in the current repository is reported, never auto-registered. Migrations never create either the operator or agent users.

commands.name: mandible user whoami [--json]
commands.description: Print the client identity the daemon resolves for the calling request: user, evidence method, credential label, and client-auth mode. Reports an unauthenticated caller rather than failing.

commands.name: mandible user list [--kind <k>] [--status <s>] [--json]
commands.description: List registry users, optionally filtered by kind (human|agent|system|external) or status (active|retired).

commands.name: mandible user show <ref> [--json]
commands.description: Resolve a user by id or slug and print it with its credentials and bindings.

commands.name: mandible user update <ref> [--name <n>] [--email <e>] [--status active|retired] [--json]
commands.description: Update mutable fields on a user (display name, email, status).

commands.name: mandible user credential add <ref> (--type <t> --fingerprint <f> [--public-material <m>] | --from-git-signingkey) [--label <l>] [--json]
commands.description: Add an immutable credential (ssh_key|yubikey_recipient|delegated_ssh_key|api_token), or derive an ssh_key credential from git user.signingkey. At most one active credential per fingerprint; no private key material is accepted.

commands.name: mandible user credential revoke <id> [--json]
commands.description: Revoke a credential. Credentials are immutable: revoke then add, never mutate a fingerprint; revoked rows keep their historical references.

commands.name: mandible user credential list <ref> [--all] [--json]
commands.description: List a user's active credentials, or all including revoked with --all.

commands.name: mandible user token mint <ref> [--label <l>] [--store [--service <name>]] [--json]
commands.description: Mint a per-user bearer token. Without --store the raw token is printed once and never again. With --store it is written straight to the OS secret store and not printed: service defaults to mandible-operator for the human operator and mandible-agent-<app> for an agent user (its shortest active app_name binding), account is the user slug, and storing again rotates the item in place. macOS keychain is the only backend today; other platforms fail visibly.

commands.name: mandible user binding add <ref> --type <t> --value <v> [--scope <s>] [--json]
commands.description: Add a claimed binding (app_name|provider_session_env|process_pattern|git_author_email|external_author). Bindings are claimed aliases only and never produce verified evidence.

commands.name: mandible user binding rm <id> [--json]
commands.description: Remove a claimed binding by id.

commands.name: mandible user binding list <ref> [--json]
commands.description: List a user's claimed bindings.

commands.name: mandible user group add|rm|members
commands.description: Create or remove custom groups and list or deliberately update idempotent group membership.

commands.name: mandible user grant add|rm|list
commands.description: Manage direct user or group project-role and global-capability grants.

commands.name: mandible user access <user> <project> [--json]
commands.description: Report a user's effective project role and global capabilities, including group grants and operator implicit admin.

trailers: Commit trailers are optional interface metadata; commits without trailers are valid but unlinked.
markdownReferences: Authored ledger Markdown issue refs use `[issue:<id>]` or `[issue:<project>/<id>]`. These refs create normal text-reference relationships.
Authored ledger Markdown comment refs use `[comment:<issue>#<comment>]` or `[comment:<project>/<issue>#<comment>]`; `[comment:#<comment>]` is a local issue UI shortcut, not a relationship-ref form.

Relationship type names such as `references`, `resolves`, `fixed_by`, `blocks`, and `tests` are `mandible issue link --type` values, not authored Markdown tags. Do not write `[references:<id>]`, `[closes:<id>]`, or similar relationship-name bracket refs.

Artifact refs are typed by meaning: `[artifact:<short-id>]` names a logical artifact, `[artifact-version:<short-id>]` pins one version, `[artifact-series:<short-id>]` follows a living series (or `[artifact-series:<short-id>@<version>]` pins its numbered version), and `[artifact-blob:<short-hash>]` names immutable bytes only. Current producers use ambiguity-safe short refs and must never emit legacy `[artifact:sha256:<hash>]` refs.

For user-facing artifact links, use `mandible artifact format <ref> --as markdown` instead of constructing routes by hand. Use `--as url`, `--as id`, or `--as full` only when that output is specifically needed; do not present a blob as though it were a logical artifact.
Auth requests have no authored Markdown bracket tag such as `[auth:<id>]`. Link them through `mandible auth request`, auth issue links, or normal issue refs when describing the related work.
authLifecycle: Protected-branch merges are asynchronous: submit an auth request, stop, and let the user approve in Mandible.
Approval and merge execution are user actions. Agents do not approve, merge, or bypass the auth queue.

Multiple pending merge requests may coexist when they are pairwise independent. Run `mandible auth check` before submitting when unsure; submission rejects clashes with file-level conflict context. Planned related branches still integrate first.

A request may carry one canonical change message: the agent authors the outcome line, a `Why:` paragraph, and optional `Caveats:`, while the CLI owns the `Merge <branch>: ` subject prefix, the `Verification:` section, and the trailers. Trailers are reference-only `Mandible-Issue:` lines for every --issue and --closes-issue ref; a canonical message never carries `Closes-Mandible-Issue:`, so closure is carried solely by the structured issue_closures field and a frozen signed message can never disagree with the authorization that runs. The daemon validates that envelope against the structured fields before digesting, stores the canonical bytes with their SHA-256, and freezes both once the request leaves pending; `mandible auth merge` verifies that digest against the exact stored bytes and commits them, or aborts. Without a message the merge keeps git's own default merge message.
coordination: The umbrella issue is the coordinator; sessions are disposable role holders.

Umbrella bodies use a canonical Children table with columns issue, scope, branch, and state; `mandible umbrella reconcile` may derive children from that table only, not from arbitrary issue refs elsewhere in the body.

Delegation manifests are stored as `delegation-manifest` checkpoints and record both `digest` (the entry's own head) and `subtree_digest` (the entry plus all transitive parent_child descendants) per entry. The first payload entry is the umbrella's own head marked `self: true` — an explicit stored self baseline, not a child entry. Refresh digests with `mandible umbrella manifest refresh <umbrella>` before resuming.

`mandible issue changed --since-issue` compares the umbrella's own issue head as well as child manifest entries, classifying each as changed, subtree_changed, unchanged, or unknown. `subtree_changed` flags work that landed on a nested sub-umbrella's descendants even when the direct child's own head is unchanged; `unknown` marks entries from manifests recorded before subtree digests existed, including the umbrella self-entry when the manifest predates the stored `self: true` baseline. Parent sessions that need their own baseline should pass `--checkpoint <id>` instead of relying on the latest shared checkpoint.
Worker closeout records `worker_status`, branch/auth pointers, blockers, and recommended next action in the child issue.

Mutating work-unit requests may carry allowlisted ambient provider identity as `{provider, provider_session_id}`; Mandible persists only those fields on work units and never stores the caller environment.

Successful auth merges archive reliably linked terminal Codex worker threads for closed child issues. Resolved work units with `provider=codex` and a provider session id can archive directly without `console_sessions`; legacy console-session links still work. Live parent-role holders and active sessions are not archived. Codex resume dispatch unarchives the provider thread before sending follow-up work.
Use `worker_status` and issue-branch links for coordination state; open/closed issue lifecycle remains separate.

The sourceable policy-free ledger mechanism client is `cli/ledger-client.sh`; it exposes work-unit, trash-custody, issue-title, session-link, issue-file, and commit-trailer helpers for policy wrappers.
transports: Default CLI transport is loopback HTTP via `MANDIBLE_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`.

Sandboxed agents without loopback can use `MANDIBLE_BASE=file:///path/to/spool` for issue, auth submission/listing, work-unit mutation, coordinator, conversation index, repo listing, and daemon-indexed log routes.
The file transport denies approval, merge, admin, and config routes; auth approval remains a user/dashboard action.
